partners.mechanism_chain: ATP2A2 (HGNC:704) —DISRUPTS→ Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity (GO:0005491); Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity (GO:0005491) —DECREASES→ Intracellular calcium ion concentration (CHEBI:29105); Intracellular calcium ion concentration (CHEBI:29105) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal keratinocyte differentiation (HP:0011223); ATP1A3 (HGNC:703) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of neuronal excitability by ion transport (GO:0090041); Regulation of neuronal excitability by ion transport (GO:0090041) —LEADS_TO→ Intracellular calcium ion concentration (CHEBI:29105); Intracellular calcium ion concentration (CHEBI:29105) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250). partners.mechanism_chain: ATP2A2 (HGNC:906) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509); Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin morphology (HP:0000949); ATP1A3 (HGNC:908) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007212); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007212) —LEADS_TO→ Paroxysmal dyskinesia (HP:0002371); Calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509) —INCREASES→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007212). Mutations in ATP2A2 impair SERCA pump function, disrupting calcium reuptuptake and thus calcium homeostasis. Dysregulated calcium homeostasis can indirectly affect neuronal excitability. **Proposed mechanism:** ATP2A2 (HGNC:704) —DISRUPTS→ ER calcium homeostasis (GO:0005974); ER calcium homeostasis (GO:0005974) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermal abnormalities (HP:0000951); ATP1A3 (HGNC:707) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204); Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar ataxia (HP:0001251); Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204) —LEADS_TO→ Areflexia (HP:0001287); Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204) —LEADS_TO→ Pes cavus (HP:0002815); Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204) —LEADS_TO→ Optic atrophy (HP:0000645); Neuronal ion homeostasis (GO:0007204) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP2A2 disrupt ER calcium homeostasis, leading to epidermal abnormalities (Darier disease). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ATP1A3 disrupt neuronal ion homeostasis, manifesting as cerebellar ataxia, areflexia, pes cavus, optic atrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss. The convergence lies in the shared cellular consequence of impaired ion homeostasis, albeit in different cell types and with distinct downstream effects.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ATP2A2 or ATP1A3 with a demonstrably opposite functional effect (e.g., gain-of-function) in patients with the respective disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. Furthermore, if patients with Darier disease present with severe neurological phenotypes identical to those in the cerebellar ataxia syndrome, and vice versa, it would suggest a more direct molecular link than currently understood. _(variant: High allele frequency (>1%) of established pathogenic variants for ATP2A2 or ATP1A3 in the general population (gnomAD) would challenge their role as causative for these rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on cellular ion homeostasis, despite arising from distinct genes, could reveal common therapeutic targets for managing epidermal and neurological dysfunction. For instance, interventions aimed at restoring calcium or sodium/potassium gradients might offer benefit across both disease contexts, or in specific affected cell types.
